issues.description: The problem specification and UML require Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String (the textual message like "Seal Clarabelle is milked") and the template/Main usage expects to print that returned message. However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with return type boolean and the implementing classes (Goat, Seal) print the message to stdout and return a boolean. This return-type mismatch will cause confusion and compilation/behavioral differences: students implementing according to the spec (String) will not match the solution, and code that prints the returned value (as in the template Main) will print boolean values instead of the intended messages.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable.messageOnMilk() signature consistent with the problem statement and template by changing its return type to String. Update the solution's Milkable interface to 'String messageOnMilk();' and modify Seal and Goat to return the formatted message (e.g., "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning a boolean. Alternatively, if boolean was intentional, update the problem statement and template Main to reflect a boolean return and to not expect the milk message string to be returned.
